messages:
Maya K: FYI customer REPORT-882 says their dedicated pool in eu-west-1 is pinning but requests are still being billed to hosted. High latency spikes noticed. Can we triage?

Josh L: Oof. Any error IDs or request IDs from the customer?

Maya K: They sent a sample request id: req_0a9f3c2e, timestamp 2026-03-01T14:22:09Z. Customer tenant: acme-enterprise-7. Dedicated pool id: ded-eu-7, region pin: eu-west-1.

Len R: Is this the usual overflow/burst path? If dedicated is saturated we should route to other dedicated hosts in region first, not hosted.

Maya K: Customer says their Dedicated pool was at ~98% and a bunch of short-lived jobs spiked. They expected fallback to other reserved nodes in the same region but saw routing to hosted and huge latencies (800-1200ms). Billing shows hosted token usage for that tenant during the incident.

Dmitri S: Can you paste the request headers and routing metadata they captured (x-region / x-routing-policy / x-fallback)?

Maya K: They collected a few headers. Snippet below (customer scrubbed):

```
x-redwood-tenant: acme-enterprise-7
x-redwood-target: model-7b
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
x-redwood-routing-policy: capacity_preferred
x-redwood-request-id: req_0a9f3c2e
x-redwood-dedicated-pool: ded-eu-7
```

Maya K: They also ran a curl with explicit region pinned and still saw a host in hosted pool:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
     -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1"
     -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate
```

Josh L: Hm. Two hypotheses: 1) pool autoscaler spilled over to hosted because overflow config allows hosted burst, 2) routing table had stale mapping where ded-eu-7 ephemeral instances were marked unhealthy and fallback policy points to hosted.

Len R: Check the routing table at the time. @ops-bot can you correlate req_0a9f3c2e to routing decisions?

ops-bot: Correlating request id req_0a9f3c2e...
ops-bot: found trace: route->region=eu-west-1 -> pool=ded-eu-7 (full) -> fallback=hosted-global -> selected=hosted-eu-1a-23 -> latency observed 970ms -> billing tag: hosted.

Dmitri S: That's the problem. The fallback policy for ded-eu-7 was misconfigured to allow hosted_global as a fallback when pool utilization >95%. Should have been fallback to ded-eu-1/2 (regional spare) or strict_block.

Maya K: Customer insists they had strict region pin set in their Console config. They show UI: "region pin: eu-west-1, fallback: regional-only".

Josh L: Two separate things: customer config vs pool-level override. We have a per-pool override that was added in an emergency last month to let inflated traffic use hosted for latency-sensitive tiers. Looks like ded-eu-7 still has that override enabled.

Len R: Why did override exist? Any change request?

Dmitri S: It was an interim fix (PR #1142) to mitigate capacity shortfalls during a hardware convoy. Should have been removed. Looks like the removal didn't apply to ded-eu-7 due to tag mismatch.

Maya K: Customer is angry because they paid hosted rates. They opened a billing dispute. Elaine (billing-bot), can you flag charges and start provisional credits?

Elaine (billing-bot): Creating billing dispute ticket BL-5519 for tenant acme-enterprise-7. Tentatively crediting overage billed to hosted during 2026-03-01T14:20:00Z - 14:40:00Z pending postmortem.

Josh L: Immediate mitigation: 1) disable hosted_global fallback for ded-eu-7 2) force re-eval routing table 3) evict ephemeral override tags. I can push the config change.

Len R: Also we should adjust autoscaler to prefer regional spare nodes and queue short jobs instead of overflow to hosted when capacity is transient. Filed infra ticket INFRA-2376.

Maya K: Can you include repro steps so we can confirm fix with customer?

Dmitri S: Repro steps I used in staging:
1) create a dedicated pool with 4 nodes, region eu-west-1, set fallback=hosted_global
2) saturate pool with parallel requests to hit >95% utilization (script attached)
3) observe routing decision in trace logs -> should pick hosted_global target
4) change pool config to fallback=regional-only, re-run spike -> observe routing to regional spare or queueing

Script (simple):
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" -d '{"input":"spam"}' https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate &
done
```

Dmitri S: In prod we saw the same pattern. After I flipped fallback to regional-only for ded-eu-7, requests routed to ded-eu-9 (regional spare) and hosted billing stopped.

Josh L: Deployed fix at 2026-03-01T15:05Z: disabled hosted_global fallback on ded-eu-7, forced routing table refresh.

ops-bot: Routing table refresh completed for pool ded-eu-7 at 2026-03-01T15:06:03Z.

Maya K: Customer confirmed reduced latency and no further hosted billing. They still want a full RCA and credits.

Len R: Root cause summary for postmortem: legacy emergency override (PR #1142) not fully reverted due to tag mismatch -> allowed hosted_global fallback when pool utilization crossed threshold -> customer region pin respected at request header level but pool fallback logic superseded -> billing and latency impact.

Dmitri S: Postmortem action items:
- Remove stale emergency overrides across all dedicated pools (INFRA-2377)
- Add an automated audit to compare customer Console fallback setting vs pool-level override and alert (ENG-PR-3890)
- Add an emergency-reversion runbook to avoid tag mismatches (SRE-22)
- Refund process: billing ticket BL-5519 (Elaine)

Elaine (billing-bot): BL-5519: provisional credit applied, will finalize after postmortem review.

Maya K: I'll keep the customer updated. Assigning owner: Josh L for immediate follow-ups, Dmitri for RCA doc.

Josh L: I'll post the short incident note to #incidents after RCA draft. :white_check_mark:

Maya K: Thanks everyone. Closing the support thread once BL-5519 is resolved. :thumbsup:

(very short follow-up 27m later)

Maya K: Customer replied: "Thanks, latency normalized and billing notice received. Please confirm the audit items so we can re-enable strict SLA pinning soon."

Josh L: I'll follow up with ETA on the audit.
